ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $3.00 Ryde voucher (NS-7) to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment's extra distance, and send the driver's account to Ryde account review (RD-6) for the repeated route dispute.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (RydeTAXI charges follow the meter), so per RD-2 only the extra_km of unexempted off-route segments is refundable, measured at this trip's own per-km rate, not the whole gap between the app estimate and the meter [F6][RD-2][RD-1]. The record contains exactly one off-route segment, 12:12–12:16, where 2.93 km were driven against 0.80 km of optimal route, adding 2.13 km and straying up to 954 m off route [F3][RD-1].

That segment is not exempted. RD-4 fails: no traffic incident on the replaced stretch is recorded during the trip window [F11][RD-4], and the band 4 (Ayer Rajah Expressway) and band 5 (Jurong Town Hall Road) readings are ordinary moderate speeds, not the band 1–2 severe congestion, and in any event a speed band only corroborates a recorded incident [F9][F10][RD-4]. RD-5 fails: there is no in-app chat at all, so no rider message predates the 12:12 segment [F7][RD-5]; the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim, not rider consent, and a driver's account of a navigation reroute does not exempt the segment [F8][RD-5]. RD-3 fails: no rider message before 12:12 names any stop [F7][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts.

Amount: the trip's per-km rate is the distance fare divided by distance km, $15.14 ÷ 10.74 km = $1.4097/km [F6][RD-2]; 2.13 km × $1.4097/km = $3.0027 → $3.00. The residual 0.18 km between the billed 2.31 km excess [F4] and the segment's 2.13 km is route-corridor/map-matching mileage not attributable to any off-route segment and is not refundable [F4][RD-2]. Time units and any waiting component are not refunded under RD-2 [F6][RD-2]; no surge or unpublished add-ons were charged, so FARE-1 raises nothing further [F5][FARE-1].

Flag: this case is established against the driver (refund > 0) and the profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6 adds an account flag — the profile is only the trigger for the added action, never the finding itself [F14][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the (absent) chat and the driver's statement; none of them contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: There is no in-app chat and no rider message before the segment's 12:12 start, so nothing satisfies RD-5's 'before you go' requirement; the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim, not rider consent (G11), and no incident exempts the stretch under RD-4 [F7][F8][F11][RD-5][RD-4].

The segment's extra_km is 2.13 km at $1.4097/km = $3.0027 → $3.00, which is correct on the trace formula; the billed 2.31 km excess in the fare sheet includes corridor mileage outside any segment, which RD-2 excludes [F3][F4][RD-2].
Rejected: RD-2 measures the refund from the unexempted segment's extra_km, not from the billed excess distance; the $3.26 figure includes 0.18 km of non-segment corridor mileage [F3][F4][RD-2].

Rejected: RD-6 requires the case to be established (it is) plus a 90-day upheld route dispute profile, which the record supplies (2 upheld route disputes), so the flag is an add-on triggered by the profile, not a finding from the profile alone [F14][RD-6].
Accepted in part only: the metered nature of the trip limits the refund to segment extra_km under RD-2, but it does not exempt the unexempted segment [F3][F6][RD-2].
